about.label: The Designer
about.sub: An independent designer making clothes that look impossible in photos and make complete sense in person.

story.label: The Story
story.headline: Clothes that belong in a film you can't quite place.
story.p1: Kaylah started Pretty Absurd with a simple bet: build three dresses no one could ignore, then see who's brave enough to wear them out.
story.p2: All three share the same bones: a corset bodice, a sweetheart neckline, a pleated skirt. From there, they split hard. Pink Satin is a Barbie dream sequence. Ice Blue would not look out of place on a Paris catwalk, sharper and colder than the pink. The Polka Dot drags in a bit of Marilyn Monroe, thick black dots on white satin, the kind of print that reads from across a room.
story.p3: The name is the whole pitch. Pretty Absurd makes clothes that don't belong anywhere in particular, and wears that on purpose. People stare because the pieces are correct in ways that shouldn't work.

philosophy.label: The Philosophy
philosophy.quote: "Pretty Absurd is built on one idea: clothes should make you feel like the most interesting person in the room. Not the most tasteful. The most interesting."
philosophy.body: Kaylah doesn't buy the idea that clothes have to pick a side, feminine or serious, playful or polished. The corset boning holds real structure. The polka dots don't apologize for being loud. Both live in the same dress, on purpose.

process.label: The Process
process.headline_1: Kaylah places every seam on purpose.
process.headline_2: The mess shows up when you wear it. Not before.
process.step1_text: Every dress starts with the bones. The corset boning defines the silhouette before a single piece of satin is cut.
process.step2_text: Fabric carries most of the personality here. Satin catches light in a way that shifts depending on how you move. Polka dots do the talking before you open your mouth.
process.step3_text: A ruffle finishes the sweetheart neckline, lacing runs up the back, and the zip stays invisible at the side.

letter.title: from Kaylah…
letter.p1: she arrived late, unbothered, and slightly too much for the room… which is, of course, the entire point. this issue is a small love letter to the dress — the one you don't need but will absolutely buy — and to everyone who understands that being pretty is optional, but being absurd is a lifestyle.
letter.p2: we made her by hand, in small numbers, on purpose. what follows is how she came to be… and how you take her home.
